MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Work out 48 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 144
   B. 1,018
   C. 1,008
   D. 998

2. Which is the best way to read the water level on a measuring jug? (1 mark)
   A. Look from high above the jug
   B. Count the number of handles
   C. Look with your eyes closed
   D. Look at the scale level with the water

3. Which number is written in words as "four thousand, six hundred and five"? (1 mark)
   A. 4,605
   B. 4,065
   C. 465
   D. 46,005

4. What is 2/3 of 21? (1 mark)
   A. 21
   B. 14
   C. 7
   D. 5

5. Change 31/10 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/10
   B. 3 2/10
   C. 1 3/10
   D. 4 1/10

6. A customer pays with Ksh 1,000 for goods that cost Ksh 750. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 240
   B. Ksh 250
   C. Ksh 350
   D. Ksh 1,750

7. What is 5 h 20 min − 2 h 35 min? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 45 min
   B. 2 h 55 min
   C. 2 h 35 min
   D. 3 h 45 min

8. Change 1,200 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 13 m
   B. 12 m
   C. 12 m 50 cm
   D. 1 m 20 cm

9. Work out 7,865 − 3,542. (1 mark)
   A. 5,323
   B. 4,223
   C. 4,323
   D. 4,333

10. Write 5/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.5
   B. 5.0
   C. 0.05
   D. 0.005

11. What should every good table have? (1 mark)
   A. A title and column headings
   B. Only pictures
   C. No numbers
   D. A long story

12. What is 5 1/4 L + 2 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/2 L
   B. 8 L
   C. 7 1/4 L
   D. 7 3/4 L

13. What is the next number in the pattern 800, 675, 550, 425, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 425
   B. 300
   C. 675
   D. 175

14. A customer pays with Ksh 1,000 for goods that cost Ksh 865. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,865
   B. Ksh 135
   C. Ksh 125
   D. Ksh 235

15. A classroom has 13 rows of 12 desks. How many desks are there? (1 mark)
   A. 156 desks
   B. 146 desks
   C. 256 desks
   D. 136 desks

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A ribbon is 1 metre long. Write 27 centimetres as a fraction of a metre and as a decimal. (3 marks)

17. A shopping list has 3 packets of rice at Ksh 130 each, 2 bottles of oil at Ksh 250 each and 1 tin of tomatoes at Ksh 60. Find the total cost. (4 marks)

18. How can you tell that a cuboid is a cube? Give one example of each from everyday life. (3 marks)

19. A lesson starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m. How long is the lesson? (3 marks)

20. Change Ksh 12 to cents and 1,250 cents to shillings. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 1,008
   48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960. 48 + 960 = 1,008.

2. D — Look at the scale level with the water
   Reading level with the water gives the correct mark.

3. A — 4,605
   four thousand, six hundred and five: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 4,605.

4. B — 14
   21 ÷ 3 = 7 and 7 × 2 = 14. So 2/3 of 21 is 14.

5. A — 3 1/10
   31 ÷ 10 = 3 remainder 1. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 1/10, so 31/10 = 3 1/10.

6. B — Ksh 250
   Change = amount paid − cost = 1,000 − 750 = Ksh 250.

7. A — 2 h 45 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 2 h 45 min.

8. B — 12 m
   1,200 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 0. So 1,200 cm = 12 m.

9. C — 4,323
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323. Check: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865.

10. C — 0.05
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 5/100 = 0.05.

11. A — A title and column headings
   A title tells what the table is about and headings tell what each column shows.

12. A — 7 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 1/4 L + 2 1/4 L = 7 1/2 L.

13. B — 300
   The rule is subtract 125. 425 − 125 = 300.

14. B — Ksh 135
   Change = amount paid − cost = 1,000 − 865 = Ksh 135.

15. A — 156 desks
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 156 desks.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: 27/100 m = 0.27 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying 1 m = 100 cm, 1 mark for 27/100, 1 mark for 0.27.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 950
   Working / marking points: 3 × 130 = 390 (1 mark); 2 × 250 = 500 (1 mark); 390 + 500 + 60 (1 mark); Ksh 950 (1 mark).

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: In a cube the length, width and height are equal. Example of a cube: a dice. Example of a cuboid that is not a cube: a matchbox or a brick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the property, 1 mark for each example.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 25 minutes
   Working / marking points: 8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours (1 mark); 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes (1 mark); total 2 h 25 min (1 mark).

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 12 = 1,200 cents; 1,250 cents = Ksh 12.50
   Working / marking points: 12 × 100 = 1,200 (1 mark); 1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so Ksh 12.50 (1 mark).
